message.text: The miss selector exports every valid in-scope miss, including `owned-missed` and `no-owner`, although the active probing decision and the base measurement contract define this measurement corpus as `needs-execution` misses.

evidence.snippet: Measuring which routes to commit, the goldens from this week's probes and the `needs-execution` misses, is the issue's second part.

- `MELIAN_EVAL_MISS_REVIEW`: `lens`, the default, reviews each miss with `trust-boundary` alone; `whole` reviews it with every lens in the base's `full` tier, as a pull request's review would, so a lens other than `trust-boundary` can find it. [Miss review cost](#miss-review-cost) gives each mode's cost.
- `MELIAN_EVAL_VERIFIER_MODEL`, required: one verifier route for every combination, keeping the golden's configured `thinking`.
- `MELIAN_EVAL_PROBE_PASSES`: passes per combination, three by default.
- `MELIAN_EVAL_PROBE_SET`: `goldens`, `misses` or `all`. It is `all` when `MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES` is set, else `goldens`.
- `MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES`: a JSON array of `{ name, repo, base, head, file, rule?, alternativeRules?, fix?, lines? }`, each a `needs-execution` miss in a clone on the machine. `fix` names the commit that fixed it; `lines` is the first and last line of the defect at the head. A sighting under `rule` or any of `alternativeRules` can find the miss. A miss may leave out `rule` only when it has `lines`, and then a sighting under any rule at those lines finds it; `alternativeRules` needs a `rule`. Each rule must be one some lens of the base's `full` tier declares for the file, in either mode, so one misses file serves both and a misspelt alternative exits 2. In `lens` mode one of them must be `trust-boundary`'s. A miss is scored on the reviewing lenses' own sightings at the head, `trust-boundary`'s in `lens` mode and every lens check's in `whole`, read from the review's store level by level, because a finding merged with another lens's, or with another level's, keeps only its speaker's lines and words. An ID excludes lines, so quick and careful can sight one ID at different lines, and the verifier can refute one and uphold the other. A sighting answers the miss when the verdict holds the claim of its check, ID and level unrefuted, it sits at the file under one of the miss's rules, or any rule when it names none, and it overlaps those lines. explanation.what: The miss selector exports every valid in-scope miss, including `owned-missed` and `no-owner`, although the active probing decision and the base measurement contract define this measurement corpus as `needs-execution` misses.
explanation.whatToDo: Require `current.reason === "needs-execution"` when producing this measurement export (and name other reasons as skipped). If broad replay is intended, record an amendment to the active probing decision and use a separately defined corpus/command contract rather than silently broadening `MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES`.
explanation.whyHere: The command writes these cases directly in the `MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES` shape. Reading misses and execution-only misses answer different questions, so adding the former silently changes the corpus used to choose probing routes and can spend live-model runs on cases outside the decided measurement.

properties.failureScenario: An unmatched external finding is adjudicated `{ verdict: "valid", reason: "owned-missed" }`, as the added test does at line 1819. This predicate includes it and `compare misses` writes it to `MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES`; the probing measurement then reviews and scores a reading failure in the corpus the active decision limits to `needs-execution` misses, producing misleading route measurements and spending a live review on the wrong case.

message.text: The new sorting changes later conclusively owned rounds from the active decision's required round-ID order to mint-time order. The edited helper is shared with membership numbering, but offline export deliberately had a different ordering rule.

evidence.snippet: Export never changes the saved snapshot or history, assigns new membership numbers, or creates a snapshot version. Saved attributed members retain their order; new owned attributed records follow in round-ID order. Raw records keep their existing order. When the selected entries actually add records beyond the snapshot-only selection, stderr names the saved version and the refresh command. Markdown also labels the snapshot's stored time and says the additional records have no snapshot numbers. A candidate without an added export record causes no warning. The notice also covers raw-only additions and makes no claim about their timestamps.

explanation.what: The new sorting changes later conclusively owned rounds from the active decision's required round-ID order to mint-time order. The edited helper is shared with membership numbering, but offline export deliberately had a different ordering rule.
explanation.whatToDo: Keep saved members in snapshot order and sort only the additional owned rounds by round ID here. Do not reuse `byMinting` for offline export unless a new active decision explicitly amends the existing ordering choice.
explanation.whyHere: `exported()` feeds both ordinary pull-request export and the new misses export. Once IDs reach values such as `r9` and `r10`, mint order and round-ID order differ, so the rendered comparison order changes and `ComparisonExport.misses()` can choose a different occurrence as the “last” one. The added test explicitly selects the order that the base decision forbids.

properties.failureScenario: A snapshot contains an older member, and offline storage later gains owned rounds `range-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.r9` (minted 09:00) and `range-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.r10` (minted 10:00). The active decision requires added records in round-ID order, which is `r10`, then `r9`; this code emits `r9`, then `r10`. If the same external ID is a miss in one and matched in the other, the misses export consequently keeps the opposite round's result from the order the repository decided.

message.text: The export flattens every report in an external-only group, turning one defect reported by several reviewers into several replay cases. The active comparison decision says each defect contributes one miss, and grouping across reviewers exists specifically to count that site once.

evidence.snippet:
- Recall counts distinct valid groups. A reviewer gets credit only for its own report judged valid. Precision counts valid reports over valid, noise, and duplicate reports.
- An unadjudicated report is pending and enters neither metric.
- An external-only group whose valid reports all say `out-of-scope` stays outside Melian's recall denominator.
- An empty denominator gives 1, with the raw counts beside it. Reviewers aggregate by name and case-folded login, ignoring version.
- Earlier rounds stay in their statistics. A repeat on a second pull request is a candidate check. `melian compare stats` counts changesets as a stand-in, so two detached rounds of one pull request can still show as a candidate: a known gap, not policy.
- Withdrawing a finding leaves its history stored but removes it from that round's summaries.
- A group with conflicting miss reasons uses the first in-scope reason in site order, falling back to `out-of-scope`. Each defect contributes one miss. Titles that normalise to no letters or digits do not form repeat clusters.
- The drain counts each changeset once. At three or more comparisons, remaining debt keeps the drain due, including after a missed threshold. Local state cannot prove which backlog pull requests shipped or which live runs passed.

**Matching.** Matching is mechanical first. An external finding matches a Melian finding in the same file whose lines overlap its own or lie within three lines of them. A Melian finding's `cause` evidence locations at head are its sites too, because an `affected` finding sits in a file the change did not edit, and a reviewer of the diff points at the changed line that breaks it. External findings from two reviewers at one site group the same way, so one defect counts once. One reviewer's two findings at one site stay two, as two reports from one check do. A finding with no line, or an outdated one, matches nothing until the maintainer matches it by hand. A hand match, or unmatch, is recorded as the maintainer's and overrides the mechanical one. Each external finding ends matched or external-only, and each Melian finding matched or Melian-only. In milestone 4 a `Decider` question, "do these name the same defect?", refines the mechanical match.

explanation.what: The export flattens every report in an external-only group, turning one defect reported by several reviewers into several replay cases. The active comparison decision says each defect contributes one miss, and grouping across reviewers exists specifically to count that site once.
explanation.whatToDo: Produce at most one replay case per external-only `ComparisonGroup`, with a deliberate rule for its name/location, or introduce a grouped export representation. Do not flatten the group's reports directly into independent misses.
explanation.whyHere: `MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES` measures cases, so duplicate reports make the same defect consume multiple live reviews and give it multiple weight in miss recall. This breaks the reason comparisons group external findings across reviewers before counting misses.

properties.failureScenario: Codex and Claude each report the same unmatched defect at `src/run.ts:12`, so `groups()` places both reports in one external-only group; both are adjudicated valid. `flatMap` emits two cases with the same repo/base/head/file/lines but different finding IDs. The measurement reviews the identical defect twice and weights it as two misses, although the active decision requires that defect to contribute one miss.
